hints.title: Horizontal Level Partitioning
hints.text: Visiting nodes row by row from top to bottom requires remembering children to inspect on the next level. How can you group nodes strictly by their depth level?

hints.title: Buffer Snapshot Invariant
hints.text: Processing all nodes currently in a first-in first-out buffer corresponds to one entire horizontal level before any of their children are processed.

hints.title: Level by Level Collection Procedure
hints.text: If root is null, return an empty list. Initialize a list of current level nodes starting with root. While the current level is not empty, collect the values of all nodes in this level, gather their non-null left and right children into the next level list, and append the values to the result.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in tree (0 <= N <= 2000)
W: maximum width of tree (up to N/2)
complexity.notes: Each node is visited once and grouped into its horizontal layer.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recursively searching for nodes at depth d for d = 0, 1, 2... requires O(N * H) time due to scanning the tree repeatedly.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Maintaining level buffers captures each level in a single pass taking O(N) time and O(W) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Clean snapshot of level length or two-array level swap, null root handling, and ordering guarantees from left to right.
